_readme: This file holds all the editable text, links, and content for the site. To change something, edit the value after the colon (the part in quotes, or the number/true/false). Do not rename anything before a colon — the code looks for those exact names — and don't remove any commas, quotes, curly braces {} or square brackets [], or the file will stop working. Any key starting with an underscore, like this one, is just a note for humans and isn't read by the site; feel free to delete them, but leaving them in place won't cause any problems.

navbar._comment: The name and two-letter badge shown in the top navigation bar.
navbar.name: Your Name

site._comment: Browser tab title and icon. If 'favicon' is a file path (e.g. '/favicon.svg'), that file is used. If it's left empty (''), an icon is generated from navbar.circleBadge using the colors below.
site.title: Your Name — Your Job Title or Specialty (shown in the browser tab)

home._comment: The introduction at the top of the page. 'primaryCta' and 'secondaryCta' are the two buttons; 'href' should point to a section id on the page, written as '#' plus that section's id (e.g. '#projects').
home.name: Your Name
home.role: Your Role · Your Specialty · Your Secondary Skill
home.tagline: HOME SECTION: A one- or two-sentence introduction. Say what you build and what tools or languages you use, so visitors understand what you do right away.

codeSnippet._comment: Powers the small 'typed code' animation. 'writes' is the list of languages it types out, three per line — add, remove, or reorder them freely. 'status' is the last line it types.

about._comment: The 'About' section. 'imagePath' is the photo shown next to the text — add the image to the project's images and put its path here. 'paragraphs' is the body text: one string per paragraph, add or remove as needed. 'facts' are the label/value rows below the paragraphs; each item needs a short 'label' and its 'value' — add or remove items freely.
about.sectionTitle: ABOUT SECTION: A headline that sums up who you are or how you work
paragraphs: ABOUT SECTION, PARAGRAPH 1: Your background. Where you studied or trained, what field you work in, and one highlight such as a key project or result.
ABOUT SECTION, PARAGRAPH 2: What you build or do outside of school or work, and what you enjoy learning.
ABOUT SECTION, PARAGRAPH 3: What you're looking for next, such as the type of role, freelance work, or collaboration you're open to.

skills.sectionDescription: SKILLS SECTION: A short intro explaining how your skills are organized and inviting visitors to pick a language to see how you use it.
skills._skillCardContentGuide: Each object in the list below is one language card. Fields: id (short, unique, lowercase — not shown on screen, just used internally); language (the big heading, e.g. 'JavaScript'); fileExtension (the small pill next to it, e.g. '.js'); color (a hex code like '#E0A800' used for that card's accent color); confidence (a number from 1 to 5 — how many bars are filled in); lineCount (how many lines the 'code' sample below produces — this must match or the line numbers won't line up); code (the snippet in the little code window, split into pieces — each piece has 'text', with \n marking where a new line starts, and 'className', which should be '' for plain text, 'text-sky-400' for keywords, 'text-amber-300' for function or class names, or 'text-emerald-400' for strings); useWith and builtWith (one sentence each, shown on the right of the card); workWith (the fileExtensions, like '.css', of related languages — these become the clickable pills that jump to that card). To add a language, copy one whole { ... } block below, including the comma before the next one, and edit every field.

projects._comment: The projects grid and its filter buttons.
projects.sectionTitle: PROJECTS SECTION: Title above the project list
projects.sectionDescription: PROJECTS SECTION: A short intro describing the kinds of projects below, such as client work, side projects, or coursework.
projects._filtersGuide: Each filter button needs a 'label' (the text on the button). The 'All' button has no 'languages' field and always shows every project. Every other button needs a 'languages' array — a project shows under that filter if any of its own 'language' values are in this list. Group languages together the way 'C / C++' does below if you want one button to match more than one language.
projects._projectListGuide: Each object below is one project card. Fields: name; description; language (an array of strings — use the exact spelling 'HTML', 'CSS', 'JS', 'JSX', 'Python', 'C', or 'C++' so the filters above match correctly); hasLive (true or false — whether to show a live-site link); liveUrl (only needed when hasLive is true); sourceUrl (link to the code); images (an array of image paths — leave it as [] to show a placeholder box instead of a photo). Each project 'name' must be unique. To add a project, copy one whole { ... } block below, including the comma before the next one, and edit every field.

projectList.name: Project 1: Web Project (HTML, CSS, JS)
projectList.description: PROJECT CARD: Two or three sentences on what the project is, what it does, and what you built. This one has a live demo link and appears under the HTML / CSS / JS filter.

projectList.name: Project 2: React Project (JSX)
projectList.description: PROJECT CARD: Two or three sentences on what the project is, what it does, and what you built. This one is tagged JSX, so it shows under the JSX filter and also under HTML / CSS / JS because it lists those languages too.

projectList.name: Project 3: Python Project
projectList.description: PROJECT CARD: Two or three sentences on what the project is, what it does, and what you built. This one has no live link (hasLive is false), so only the Source Code button appears in its preview.

projectList.name: Project 4: C Project
projectList.description: PROJECT CARD: Two or three sentences on what the project is, what it does, and what you built. This one appears under the C / C++ filter.

projectList.name: Project 5: Mixed C / C++ Project
projectList.description: PROJECT CARD: Two or three sentences on what the project is, what it does, and what you built. This one lists both C and C++ as its languages.

projectList.name: Project 6: Small Layout Exercise
projectList.description: PROJECT CARD: Two or three sentences on what the project is, what it does, and what you built. Good for coursework, challenges, and short exercises.

contact._comment: The closing section. 'email', 'github', 'linkedin' and 'facebook' show as contact links — 'github', 'linkedin' and 'facebook' should be full links starting with https://. 'formNote' is the small print shown under the message form.
contact.sectionTitle: CONTACT SECTION: Title above the contact details
contact.sectionDescription: CONTACT SECTION: A short invitation to get in touch, including how quickly you reply.
contact.formNote: CONTACT FORM NOTE: Small print under the message form, such as what happens when the visitor presses send.
